title: Batteries' Vector.scanrM: compiled implementation disagrees with its definition
summary: In Batteries, Vector.scanrM is @[implemented_by] scanrMFast, whose loop stored the accumulator from before folding in the current element instead of the new one, so every entry of the compiled result was off by one fold: Vector.scanr (· + ·) 0 #v[1, 2, 3] gave [5, 3, 0, 0] instead of [6, 5, 3, 0]. #eval and compiled code returned wrong answers, and since native_decide trusts the compiled code while the kernel uses the definition, the two prove False. Not a kernel bug: #print axioms shows the native_decide axiom. Fixed in the Batteries release for Lean v4.33.0 (first in v4.33.0-rc2).
